headline: Approved minutes of a prior meeting unanimously, and discussed delays in the 2023 town audit with CBIZ and Claremont.
summary: Members discussed the 2023 audit requests from CBIZ, reconciliations of Board of Education accounts, and Claremont's expired contracts. No finalized variances were reported. Members approved the minutes of the previous meeting unanimously.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 8, 2026 meeting, passed unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion to approve minutes made by Council member Figlar; Seconded by Vice Chair Alston. Vote: Motion passed unanimously.

plain_text:
TOWN OF 
HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
 
 
 
AUDIT COMMITTEE 
 
 
 
 
Committee Chair: 
Present - Sarah Gallagher, Legislative Council Majority 
Leader 
Committee Members: 
Absent - Katie Kiely, Legislative Council President 
Absent - Bob Anthony, Legislative Council Minority 
Leader 
Present - Jeron Alston 
Present - Rhonda Caldwell 
Alternates 
Present - Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
Present - Tasha Hunt, Majority Whip 
Present - Tom Figlar, Minority Whip 
 
 
 
   
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL 
Audit Committee Special Meeting, October 21, 2026 – 6:00pm.  Vice Chair Jeron Alston 
called the meeting to order at 6:35pm with the members noted above in attendance. 
 
2. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION 
No one came forward to give public input.  Public Input was closed at 6:39pm. 
  
3. INFORMATION ITEMS 
  1. Progress Update from the Administration – 
 
The Administration provided an overview of the process for preparing and reviewing 
documentation requested by CBIZ. Materials are prepared by staff, reviewed by the 
Deputy Finance Director and Finance Director, and returned to staff for submission 
through Suralink. Approximately 22 items had been uploaded since the previous 
week, with a number of requests completed or reviewed and others remaining open. 
 
Work continues on cash reconciliations. Bank statements that were not previously 
available have been obtained and are being compared with existing reconciliations. 
The General Fund, as the Town's major account, is expected to require additional 
time.  
 
Budget Liaison Pascarella questioned why discrepancies between the 2023 and 
2024 accounts had not been addressed earlier. It was explained that CBIZ had 
identified the issue and maintained an outstanding request for information for 
approximately two years. It was also noted that this information had previously been 
disclosed publicly through the Finance Commission. 
 
Councilwoman Rhonda Caldwell requested that timelines and deadlines be 
established. The Administration explained that many outstanding items have due 
dates, while others involve issues requiring resolution, making completion dates more 
difficult to estimate. Ms. Caldwell reiterated her request that CLA include timelines 
and deadlines for outstanding items in its reports to the Legislative Council and the 
public.
Council member Figlar noted efforts to arrange a meeting with Claremont, suggesting 
that multiple meetings may be necessary. A request was made to establish regularly 
scheduled meetings following the initial discussion. 
 
The Committee discussed Claremont's prior contracts, which expired in June 2026, 
and questions regarding the firm's responsibility to provide information and 
assistance related to work previously performed. Concerns were expressed about 
incurring additional charges for services or information that may already be covered 
under the original agreements. The Administration indicated that it is reviewing the 
contractual issues, actively working toward a resolution, and keeping Legislative 
Council leadership informed. 
  
  2. Items Going from Administration to CBIZ on 23 Audit 
This information was provided during the Administration’s Progress Update under 
item 1.  
  
  3. Update on BOE 
Board of Education COO Tom Ariola provided an update on the reconciliation of BOE 
accounts. He explained that the BOE's payroll and accounts payable accounts had 
reconciled with the Town prior to the 2023 audit. Following the audit, four adjusting 
entries were identified, but the BOE was able to locate supporting documentation for 
only two. Information regarding the remaining two adjustments was needed from 
Claremont in order to reconcile the accounts with the General Ledger. 
 
Mr. Ariola explained that the BOE performs reconciliations and submits its 
adjustments, but the Town had not been performing corresponding reconciliations. 
He noted that final audit adjustments had not been shared between the BOE and 
Town. 
 
Separate meetings between Claremont and the BOE and between Claremont and the 
Town were being scheduled. Council member Jeron Alston requested that the BOE 
keep the Council informed of its meetings. There was also a request for the BOE, 
Town, and auditors to meet jointly to ensure that all parties were working from the 
same information. 
 
Mr. Ariola emphasized the importance of obtaining and agreeing upon final audit 
adjustments before proceeding with subsequent years. He indicated that the BOE 
and Town are working together and intend to continue doing so until the outstanding 
matters are resolved, after which a new process will be followed. He also noted that 
the new auditors expect the preparation of trial balances and journal entries to be 
handled by the Town and BOE and will provide recommendations regarding the 
process. 
  
  4. Any Finalized Variances 
The Committee was advised that there are no finalized variances at this time. It was 
noted that finalized variances are expected to be made public, and a request was 
made that details of the larger variances also be shared with the public.
4. ACTION ITEMS 
 
  1. Approval of Minutes from the October 8, 2026 Meeting 
Motion to approve minutes made by Council member Figlar; Seconded by Vice Chair 
Alston.  
Vote: Motion passed unanimously. 
5. UNFINISHED COMMITTEE BUSINESS 
 
  1. Update on Plan for Out Year Audits (24 Audit and Beyond) 
It was explained that Out Year audits could not be considered until the 2023 audit is 
completed. The Town is currently addressing requests from CBIZ for 2023, and once the 
auditors are satisfied with the 2023 figures, work will move to the 2024 audit. 
 
In response to a Council member's question, the Director acknowledged that many of the 
same challenges encountered with the 2023 audit are anticipated with subsequent years, 
particularly with reconciliations that had not been performed and will need to be created. 
He explained, though, that as information is requested from third parties for the 2023 
audit, the Town is also requesting information for subsequent years to avoid duplicating 
those efforts and help expedite future audits. 
 
There was also discussion regarding the requirement to change auditors every six years,  
with the observation that the current auditors have not yet completed an audit. 
 
  
6. NEW COMMITTEE BUSINESS 
 
  1. Expected Due Dates for Next Meeting 
The next meeting will be November 4, 2026 
  2. Additional Items 
There were no additional items for this evening’s meeting. 
  
7. ADJOURN  
Vice Chair Alston made a motion to adjourn, Council member Figlar seconded.  All were in 
favor, and the meeting was adjourned at 7:37pm.
